issues.legal_issue: The Supreme Court had jurisdiction to hear an appeal from a pre-Constitution High Court decree under the Federal Court’s transitional appellate jurisdiction.
material_facts: The High Court reversed the trial court’s decree in a civil property suit before the Constitution came into force.
The value of the property exceeded the threshold that then permitted an appeal to the Federal Court, and the appellants applied for leave to appeal before the Constitution came into force.
The High Court granted leave after the Constitution came into force.
The appeal had not yet been admitted by the Federal Court when the Constitution came into force.
issues.conclusion: Article 133 did not govern an appeal from the pre-Constitution decree, but the appeal was competent under Article 135 because the Federal Court’s jurisdiction over such an appeal was exercisable when the decree was made and the required conditions were met.
issues.legal_principle: Article 133 applies to appeals from judgments, decrees, or final orders of a High Court in the territory of India, meaning a State High Court under the Constitution, and did not apply to this pre-Constitution decree. Under Article 135, the Supreme Court retains jurisdiction over a matter if the Federal Court’s jurisdiction and powers in relation to it were exercisable immediately before the Constitution commenced under existing law. Jurisdiction was exercisable once the decree giving rise to the appeal existed, subject to applicable conditions; it did not depend on the appeal already being pending or formally admitted. Article 374(2) addresses pending matters, while paragraph 20 of the Adaptation of Laws Order, 1950, as amended in 1951, preserved accrued rights. The Court considered but distinguished Gundapuneedi Veeranna v. Gundapuneedi China Venkanna, where both the decree and the application for leave post-dated the Constitution.

predicates.civil_appeal_from_preconstitution_decree: A party brings a civil appeal from a High Court decree made before the constitutional appellate court system began.
predicates.federal_appeal_right_accrued_under_exist: Existing law gave the party a right to appeal to the former federal court from the decree, subject to applicable procedural conditions.
predicates.decree_exceeded_former_appeal_value_thre: The value of the dispute exceeded the value threshold that permitted an appeal to the former federal court.

issues.definition: When a civil appeal challenges a pre-transition decree and the former federal court had appellate jurisdiction over it under existing law because the value threshold was met, the appeal is competent under the transitional jurisdiction.

issues.legal_issue: A deed transferring specified property in exchange for rights in other property conveyed the specified property outright when its terms did not make the transfer temporary or conditional.
material_facts: A deed allocated specified land to a family branch in exchange for that branch’s share of income and property rights elsewhere.
The deed stated that the transferors had no inheritance claim over the allocated land.
Possession of part of the land was delayed because it was subject to a mortgage, but the deed did not say that the land would be returned when possession of the other property became available.
The defendants’ branch had possessed the disputed land as owners since the deed was made.
The plaintiff sought possession of the land, claiming it had been given only provisionally or for maintenance.
issues.conclusion: The deed effected an unconditional transfer of the disputed land; the plaintiff’s claim to recover it was baseless, and the trial court’s dismissal of the suit was restored.
issues.legal_principle: The Court construed the deed according to its plain terms. Its allocation of identified land in exchange for rights in other property, and its express relinquishment of inheritance claims, did not support treating the transfer as provisional or conditional. A delay in possession caused by a mortgage did not imply a right to recover the land later, and a return condition could not be read into the deed contrary to its terms.

rule.if: property_possession_suit and deed_allocated_specific_land_in_exchange and deed_disclaimed_transferors_inheritance_claim and deed_delayed_possession_due_to_mortgage and deed_stated_no_return_condition

predicates.property_possession_suit: A party brings a suit seeking possession of disputed property.
predicates.deed_allocated_specific_land_in_exchange: A deed allocated identified land to one branch in exchange for that branch’s rights or income in other property.
predicates.deed_disclaimed_transferors_inheritance_: The deed stated that the transferors retained no inheritance claim over the allocated land.
predicates.deed_delayed_possession_due_to_mortgage: The deed explained that possession of some allocated land was delayed because the land was mortgaged.
predicates.deed_stated_no_return_condition: The deed contained no term requiring the allocated land to be returned when possession of other property became available.

issues.definition: When a possession suit concerns land allocated by deed in exchange for rights elsewhere, the deed disclaims the transferors’ inheritance claim, delayed possession is explained by a mortgage, and the deed states no return condition, the claim to recover the transferred land is rejected.
